explain.say: Do onions make you cry every time? When you cut an onion, you burst its tiny cells, and they let out a gas that stings your eyes, so your eyes make tears to wash it away. Let's learn a routine to beat it! Look at the first step: chill the onion in the fridge for about 30 minutes.

explain.say: Why does cold help? The stinging gas is made by a chemical reaction, and cold slows reactions down. A cold onion also lets less gas float up into the air. Do you remember another way cold helps in the kitchen?

faq.q: Why does chilling an onion help?
faq.a: The stinging gas comes from a chemical reaction when cells burst. Cold slows the reaction and stops the gas floating up so quickly.
asks: Does putting onions in the fridge stop crying?

faq.q: Why does a sharp knife help with onions?
faq.a: A sharp knife cuts cleanly through fewer cells, so less stinging gas comes out. A blunt knife crushes many cells.
asks: Does a blunt knife make you cry more?

faq.q: Why do onions make you cry?
faq.a: Cutting bursts the onion's cells, which make a gas called syn-propanethial-S-oxide. It reaches your eyes and stings, so your eyes make tears to wash it away.
asks: What gas comes out of onions?

faq.a: Yes, close-fitting goggles that seal around your eyes keep the gas out. Ordinary glasses help only a little.
asks: Do swimming goggles help when cutting onions?

faq.q: Is there an onion that doesn't make you cry?
faq.a: Yes. Plant breeders have made tearless onions, such as Smile Ball in Japan and Sunions in the USA.

facts: Cutting onions releases syn-propanethial-S-oxide, a gas that irritates the eyes.
Chilling an onion slows the reactions that produce the eye-stinging gas.
